LocalizedText cleanup is one of the nested clear routines reached from Variant deletion and can free string members embedded in decoded values.
The generic clear dispatcher invokes the type-specific clear function for the decoded object graph, releasing heap storage owned by the Variant.
If the decoded object graph contains an internal alias or double-owned member, the clear path can free it while another reference still exists.
The root cause hypothesis is that JSON decoding can leave a Variant with ownership metadata that causes later cleanup to free memory still reachable through another nested reference.
A subsequent clear of a nested LocalizedText/String member can then read from or free the already-released heap region, producing the reported use-after-free sink.
